result.title: ORGANIC3D: Grounding 3D CT Vision Language Models in Organ Level Image Text Coupling
result.summary: Vision language models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance in 3D computed tomography (CT) classification, but high accuracy does not reflect whether their predictions rely on the correct anatomical evidence. We introduce ORGANIC3D, a framework for evaluating and improving organ level image text alignment through controlled anatomical interventions. Our benchmark assesses 12 vision encoder checkpoints and 7 generative VLMs using matched patient comparisons, organ erasure, lesion replacement, and laterality perturbations, revealing substantial alignment failures even among top performing models. To learn organ level image text correspondence, ORGANIC3D aligns each finding sentence with the anatomy aware image features and trains on edited scans to anchor this alignment in the organ's image evidence. We further extend this framework to generative VLMs, promoting evidence dependent question answering and report generation. Trained exclusively on public data, ORGANIC3D achieves SOTA classification AUROC on CTRATE, Merlin, and the heldout RADChestCT dataset and reaches 77% laterality accuracy, compared with at most 66% for prior models. Its generative VLM matches or exceeds all evaluated publicly released VLMs on visual question answering, achieves the highest report accuracy, and retracts 96 to 99% of target organ findings after organ removal, versus a maximum of 69% for other models. Together, these results establish ORGANIC3D as a framework for testing whether 3D CT vision language models ground their predictions in anatomical evidence and for improving organ level alignment alongside predictive accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ORGANIC3D，用器官擦除、病灶替换、左右侧扰动等受控解剖干预，检验 3D CT 视觉语言模型的预测是否真正依赖正确的器官级图像证据，并通过将发现句子与解剖感知图像特征对齐、在编辑后扫描上训练来改善这种证据依赖，同时扩展到生成式 VQA 与报告生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是用干预与证据撤回来区分「看图」与「视觉旁路」，与关注的答案是否使用视觉证据、证据筛选与贡献分配直接对应，可供核查如何把这类因果干预用于 LVR 的 latent 状态诊断与训练监督。
